AirdromeRef.description:
An airdrome as a request names it: a number is its id; a string is its
`name_id` or, where no `name_id` matches, its id written in digits.

Alternative.description: One alternative: a full route, and how it relates to the others.

chokepoints.description:
Edges of this route in the top decile of their network's
betweenness; null while betweenness is still being built.

length.description: Planar length of the road geometry.

overlap_with.description: Shared length fraction against each other returned route, in order.

shared_edges_with_all.description:
Edges along which every alternative runs: the pair's true
chokepoints.

straight_line.description:
The distance between the endpoints, so `length / straight_line` is the
detour factor.

waypoints.description: At most one point per 500 m, and every graph node kept.

geojson.description: Also return each blind arc as a wedge in GeoJSON.

radius.description: The engagement or search radius each radial is marched in from.

resolution.description:
Raster cell size; the file's cell size when omitted, and may be
coarser.

sector.description: Summaries are also returned restricted to this sector.

bands.description: One per requested band, in order.

geojson.description:
A wedge per blind arc out to `radius`, with the site, when `geojson`
was asked for.

Box.description: An axis-aligned box in DCS metres, the canonical region.

CacheEntry.description:
One cache entry: `current`, `missing`, or `stale` with the reason.
`size` is its file's bytes, null when there is none.

tpi_300_mean.description:
Mean `tpi_300` along the edge's geometry, null where no sample has
ground.

geojson.description: Also return the answer as GeoJSON.

region.description: Edges any point of whose path lies in it.

edges.description: Highest betweenness first, ties in edge order.

geojson.description: Each edge, when `geojson` was asked for.

Counts.description:
How many of each thing the terrain holds. The tables' counts are always
given; road edges and scenery objects are null until a request in the
same process has read the road graph or the scenery.

asset_covered_fraction.description: Present when the request named an `asset`.

blind_approach_exists.description:
Some radial stays masked from the envelope's radius to inside
`min_masked_range`.

asset.description: An area whose coverage is reported on its own.

geojson.description: Also return the dead zones as GeoJSON.

resolution.description: Mask cell size; the file's cell size when omitted, and may be coarser.

bands.description: One per requested band, in order.

geojson.description:
Each band's dead zones as one `MultiPolygon`, the site, and the
asset's outline when given, when `geojson` was asked for.

Criterion.description:
One criterion, written `{"name": "slope_max", "params": {"deg": 8}}`.
`valid` takes no params and is applied whether asked for or not.

oneOf.description: Steepest slope over the footprint, at most `deg`.

Highest minus lowest height over the footprint's corners and centre,
at most `m`.
Every footprint cell's water class is one of `classes`.
Every footprint cell's `surface` code is one of `values`.
Every footprint cell's ground cover is one of `classes`.

The share of the covered cells within `radius` that are of `class`,
at least `min`.
Distance to the nearest cell of `class`, from `min` to `max`.

Distance to the nearest airdrome, or to `airdrome` when given: its id
as a number, or its `name_id`.
Scenery objects of `class` within `radius`, at most `max`.
Scenery objects overlapping the footprint, at most `max`.

Objects of any class within `radius`: what a heliport static would
remove at spawn.

A ridge that way: every horizon bin in the sector rises at least
`min_elev_deg`.

The fraction of `observers` that can see the site at `own_alt_agl`,
at most `max_fraction`.

The fraction of `targets` the site sees from `own_alt_agl`, at least
`min_fraction`.

The site's landform class is one of `classes`, judged at
`threshold_m` of local and regional relief.

DescribeResponse.description: What a terrain is, which files answer for it, and how much of it is known.

cache.description:
Each cache entry as it stands; empty for the synthetic terrain,
which has no cache.

extent.description: The box the terrain's cells cover; null until its mesh has been read.

files.description: Each terrain file a decoder reads, as its header states it.

validation.description: The last live validation's figures; null when none has run.

geojson.description: Also return the candidates and their footprints as GeoJSON.

spacing.description: No two candidates returned are closer than this.

step.description: Candidate lattice spacing; twice the cell size when omitted.

weights.description: Weight per criterion name in the ranking sum; 1 for any not named.

geojson.description: Each candidate and its footprint, when `geojson` was asked for.

seen_fraction.description:
The share of the cells within `radius` with ground whose floor is at
or below `alt_agl`.

FloorRaster.description:
Laid out as `viewshed`'s mask: `height` rows running north, each
`width` cells running east, from the corner at `origin_x`, `origin_z`.
Each layer is one little-endian `f32` per cell, base64 encoded, NaN
where a cell's center lies beyond `radius` or has no ground.

floor_agl.description:
The lowest height above the cell's ground at which the site sees a
target.

floor_msl.description: The same as an altitude above sea level.

Footprint.description: A rectangle to be placed, tried at each of its orientations.

GeoPoint.description:
A position in WGS84 degrees, with its MGRS reference to the meter; the
reference is null outside 80° S to 84° N, where MGRS uses polar grids.

GeoResponse.description: Each list in the order of the request's.

Issue.description:
One thing wrong with a request or with the file it was asked of. An
operation returns a full result or a list of these, never a partial.

code.description: Stable, machine-readable: `snake_case`, never reworded once shipped.

path.description:
Where in the request, dotted: `criteria.2.params.deg`. Empty when the
issue is not about one field.

edge_id.description:
The graph edge the leg runs along, all of it or, at an end of the
route, part.

exposure.description: The fraction of the leg the exposure observers see.

Nearby.description:
For road and rail, the closest point on each of the nearest edges, `id`
being the edge's index in the graph and `class` its road class. A node
result's `kind` is `node_red` or `node_blue`, the side whose position it
gives. A scenery object's `class` is its scenery class and `name` its
model.

NearestKind.description: `node` matches both sides' nodes; each result's `kind` says which.

class.description:
For `kind` `scenery`, only objects of this class; `effect` objects
are found only when named here.

Network.description: A road network an operation runs over.

Observer.description: Someone looking: a position and an eye height above the ground.

Point3.description:
A point with a height, given either absolute or above the ground.

Exactly one of `alt` and `alt_agl` is set; `Point3::check` reports both or
neither as an issue. The pair is two fields rather than an enum so the JSON
reads `{"x": .., "z": .., "alt_agl": 2}`, the way a caller writes it.

PointFloor.description: A point's floor; the floors are null beyond `radius` or off the mesh.

Polygon.description: A simple polygon as `[x, z]` vertices, closed by its first point.

bands_agl.description: The heights above ground the bands are drawn at.

geojson.description: Also return the bands, or the points, as GeoJSON.

points.description: Answer at these points instead of over a raster.

resolution.description:
Raster cell size; the file's cell size when omitted, and may be
coarser.

RadarFloorResponse.description: The floor is a raster without `points`, and one row per point with them.

bands.description: The share of the raster's cells seen at each band, lowest first.

geojson.description:
One `MultiPolygon` per band, lowest first, or a `Point` per point,
with the site, when `geojson` was asked for.

blind.description: Masked from the radius in to `min_masked_range`.

unmask_dist.description:
The range of the first step the site sees; null when the whole radial
is masked.

Region.description:
A region a request is bounded by. Each form is converted to its bounding
box plus a membership test before any grid is read.

oneOf.description: The ring between two distances from an airdrome's reference point.

avoid.description: No edge crossing any of these is used.

exposure_observers.description: Edges these observers see cost more, by `exposure_weight`.

geojson.description: Also return the answer as GeoJSON.

max_detour_factor.description:
No route longer than this times the straight line between the
snapped ends, or 5 km longer when that is more, is searched for.

max_overlap.description: No two alternatives share more than this fraction of their length.

max_stretch.description: No alternative longer than this times the shortest.

penalty.description: The weight multiplier on edges already used.

geojson.description:
Each route, the edges they all share and the ends, when `geojson`
was asked for.

routes.description:
The least-cost route first, which with no exposure weight is the
shortest, then the alternatives in the order found.

avoid.description: No edge crossing any of these is used.

exposure_observers.description: Edges these observers see cost more, by `exposure_weight`.

geojson.description: Also return the answer as GeoJSON.

max_detour_factor.description:
No route longer than this times the straight line between the
snapped ends, or 5 km longer when that is more, is searched for.

RouteResponse.description: The route found, with the file that answered.

geojson.description: The route, each leg and the ends, when `geojson` was asked for.

length.description: Planar length of the road geometry.

straight_line.description:
The distance between the endpoints, so `length / straight_line` is the
detour factor.

waypoints.description: At most one point per 500 m, and every graph node kept.

RouteSpan.description: A stretch of a route, as distances along it from its first point.

max_rows.description: More rows than this is an error, never a truncated answer.

step.description: Lattice spacing inside `region`, at least the cell size.

distance_capped.description: Some distance found nothing within its cap and reads as the cap.

SampleRow.description:
Over a region, `height` is bilinear between cell centers and every other
layer the cell holding the point; at given points, the ground layers are
the mesh triangle's own and the derived layers the cell's. A value is
null where the layer is undefined.

SceneryInRequest.description:
Either `region`, or `footprint_at` for exact overlap with a placed
footprint.

classes.description:
Only objects of these classes; every class but `effect` when
omitted.

max_rows.description: More objects than this is an error, never a truncated answer.

SceneryObject.description:
An object's box is `obb_w` across its local x axis, which points
`rotation_deg` from north towards east, and `obb_d` across its local z;
both are null for a model with no footprint. `alt` is its base and
`height` its model's top above that.

geojson.description: Also return the site and its footprint as GeoJSON.

ScoreSiteResponse.description:
The site at its best orientation: one that passes every hard test if
any does, the highest score among those, the first given on a tie.

geojson.description: The site and its footprint, when `geojson` was asked for.

score.description:
The sum of the term scores, as `find_sites` ranks with every weight
1.

Sector.description: An arc of bearings, clockwise from `from_deg` to `to_deg`.

sector_summary.description: The same summaries over the requested `sector` only.

Term.description:
One criterion's contribution: the measured `value`, whether the hard test
passed, and the soft score from 0 to 1.

TerrainFile.description: One terrain file, its path relative to the install.

class.description:
The class and format version the container header names; null for
Lua source and `assets.assets`, which have no header.

TpiClass.description:
A landform class from local relief, then regional relief, then slope:
the first that holds of `ridge`, `valley`, `upper`, `lower`, `mid`, and
`flat` otherwise.

geojson.description: Also return the answer as GeoJSON.

max_slope_deg.description: Steeper ground than this blocks; at most 60.

TrafficabilityResponse.description:
Judged along the straight line to the nearest road, sampled every 25 m
for slope and water.

blocking.description: The first sample that fails, when one does.

cost.description:
The line's length weighted by how hard its ground is to cross, in
meters of open flat ground; null when it is not reachable.

geojson.description:
The line, its ends and the blocking point, when `geojson` was asked
for.

reason.description: Why the line is or is not passable, for a reader.

geojson.description:
Also return the route, its masked stretches and the first-seen
point as GeoJSON.

first_seen.description:
Where along the route the site first sees it, with an absolute
`alt`; null when never.

Validation.description: The figures a live validation sortie measured against the running sim.

los_agreement.description: The share of sightlines on which `visible` agreed with the sim.

route_ratio.description: Route length over the sim's own route length.

geojson.description: Also return the visible area as GeoJSON.

resolution.description: Mask cell size; the file's cell size when omitted, and may be coarser.

ViewshedResponse.description:
The mask is `height` rows running north, each `width` cells running
east, from the corner at `origin_x`, `origin_z`; cell `(row, col)` is bit
`row × width + col`, most significant first within each byte, base64
encoded. A set bit is a cell whose center lies within `radius` and at
which a target `target_alt_agl` above the ground is seen.

geojson.description:
The visible area as one `MultiPolygon`, with the observer, when
`geojson` was asked for.

rings.description:
The outlines of the set cells as `[x, z]`, north then east, when
`as_polygons` was asked for: each polygon counterclockwise on a map,
then the holes in it clockwise, so a hole is told by its winding.

visible_fraction.description:
The share of the cells within `radius` that have ground which are
seen.

geojson.description: Also return the answer as GeoJSON.

blocking.description: The first terrain point in the way, with an absolute `alt`.

clearance_m.description:
The least vertical gap between sightline and terrain; negative when
blocked.

geojson.description:
The sightline, its ends and the blocking point, when `geojson` was
asked for.
